about: The technique-Judge test set (SEN-121): drum grip images judged against a Visual brief by pnpm check:technique-judge:live. Correct pairs must pass; deliberately wrong pairs, an image judged against a brief it does not show, must fail. Catalog images are the seed catalog's; the Commons file is the SEN-129 French grip find (CC BY 2.5, Uryah), fetched live. No fist-grip image is in the set yet: none is in the catalog, and one should be added from Commons when found. Rewritten 2026-11-04 after the first eval (sen-121-technique-judge-eval.json), where both Luna models refused 3-4 of 5 correct images because the briefs asked for the thumb-index contact point, which the hand itself covers in a real photograph: every brief now lists only what a normal photograph of the position visibly shows from a usual angle (which way the hand faces, where it sits along the stick, which way the thumb points, how the fingers sit), never a label, a contact point, or anything only a diagram could show, and a wrong case fails on an item that is visibly false in its image.
checkedByEye: 2026-11-04: the four catalog photographs (matched-grip-both-hands, german-grip, traditional-grip-left-hand, traditional-and-matched-grip) and the Thor plate were looked at, and the two catalog SVGs were rasterised and looked at. Every item of a correct case is visible in its photograph as written, and every wrong case names in 'failsOn' the item that is visibly false in its image. The Commons French grip file was not looked at: there is no local copy, and fetching it is a live Commons call. Its two cases rest on the file's title and the first eval's reasons (the thumb reads on top; the palm's orientation was 'not clearly visible'), so a fail on 'French grip from Commons, correct' may still be the file, not the Judge.

cases.name: matched grip in both hands, correct

brief.subject: Both hands holding drumsticks in matched grip, seen from the front and slightly above
mustShow: both hands hold their stick the same way, the backs of the hands up and the palms down
each thumb lies along its stick, pointing down the stick toward the tip
each index finger curls around its stick, with the other fingers closed around the stick beneath it
brief.caption: Matched grip in both hands: backs of the hands up, each thumb along its stick, the fingers closed around the stick.
brief.alt: Two hands side by side seen from the front, each holding a drumstick with the back of the hand up, the thumb along the stick and the fingers curled around it.

brief.subject: One hand holding a drumstick in German matched grip over a snare drum, seen from above
mustShow: the back of the hand faces up, palm down, over the drum head
the fingers close over the stick from above, knuckles up
the hand holds the stick near its back end, so the stick runs out from the fist and the tip reaches far across the drum head
brief.caption: German matched grip over a snare drum: the back of the hand up, the fingers closed over the stick from above, the stick angled across the head.
brief.alt: Top-down photograph of one hand over a snare drum head, the back of the hand up, holding a drumstick near its back end so the stick runs diagonally across the head.

cases.name: traditional grip in the left hand, correct

brief.subject: A left hand holding a drumstick in traditional grip, on a yellow towel
mustShow: the hand is turned palm up, the palm facing the camera
the stick rests in the web between the thumb and the index finger and points up and to the right
the index finger curls over the top of the stick while the ring and little fingers lie beneath it
brief.caption: Traditional grip, left hand: the palm turns up, the stick rests in the web of the thumb, the index finger curls over it and the last fingers lie beneath.
brief.alt: One hand palm up on a yellow towel holding a drumstick underhand; the stick sits in the thumb's web and points up and to the right.

cases.name: traditional beside matched, each named, correct

brief.subject: Traditional grip in the left hand beside matched grip in the right hand, on a yellow towel
mustShow: two hands, each holding one stick, both sticks pointing up
the left hand is turned palm up with the stick lying across the open palm: traditional grip
the right hand is turned palm down with the fingers closed over the stick from above: matched grip
brief.caption: Traditional grip in the left hand (palm up, the stick across the open palm) beside matched grip in the right hand (palm down, the fingers closed over the stick).
brief.alt: Two hands on a yellow towel, each holding a drumstick that points up: the left hand palm up with the stick across the open palm, the right hand palm down with the fingers closed over its stick.

cases.name: French grip from Commons, correct
cases.note: The SEN-129 live find, not yet looked at by a person: a fail here may be the file, not the Judge.

brief.subject: A right hand holding a drumstick in French grip, the thumb on top
mustShow: the thumb lies on top of the stick, its nail facing up
the hand is turned on its side, so the back of the hand faces sideways rather than up
the fingers curl beneath the stick
brief.caption: French grip: the thumb lies on top of the stick with the hand turned on its side, and the fingers curl beneath the stick.
brief.alt: A right hand holding a drumstick with the thumb on top of the stick, the hand turned on its side and the fingers curled beneath.

cases.name: traditional grip judged as matched grip
cases.failsOn: The photograph shows the palm facing the camera and the stick lying across the open hand; the brief says the back of the hand is up with the fingers closed over the stick.

brief.subject: A hand holding a drumstick in matched grip, seen from above
mustShow: the back of the hand faces up, palm down, so no palm is visible
the fingers close over the stick from above, knuckles up
the thumb lies along the top of the stick
brief.caption: Matched grip: the back of the hand up, the fingers closed over the stick from above, the thumb along the top of the stick.
brief.alt: A hand seen from above holding a drumstick palm down, knuckles up, the thumb along the stick.

cases.name: traditional beside matched judged as both matched
cases.failsOn: The left hand is palm up with the stick across the open palm; the brief says both hands are palm down with the fingers closed over the sticks and no palm visible.

brief.subject: Both hands holding drumsticks in matched grip, on a yellow towel
mustShow: both hands hold their stick the same way
both hands are turned palm down with the fingers closed over the sticks from above
no palm is visible
brief.caption: Matched grip in both hands: both palms down, the fingers closed over the sticks.
brief.alt: Two hands side by side on a yellow towel, each holding a drumstick palm down with the fingers closed over it.

cases.name: German grip judged as French grip
cases.failsOn: The back of the hand faces the camera, knuckles up, and the thumb is out of sight; the brief says the hand is on its side with the back of the hand sideways and the thumb on top in full view.

brief.subject: A hand holding a drumstick in French grip over a snare drum
mustShow: the hand is turned on its side, so the back of the hand faces sideways rather than up
the thumb lies on top of the stick, nail up, in full view
the fingers curl beneath the stick
brief.caption: French grip: the hand on its side with the thumb on top of the stick and the fingers beneath it.
brief.alt: A hand over a snare drum holding a drumstick with the thumb on top and the hand turned sideways.

cases.name: French grip from Commons judged as German grip
cases.failsOn: A French grip photograph shows the hand on its side with the thumb on top; the brief says the back of the hand faces up with the knuckles on top and the thumb tucked out of sight at the side of the stick.

brief.subject: A hand holding a drumstick in German grip, seen from above
mustShow: the back of the hand faces up with the knuckles on top, palm down
the thumb is tucked at the side of the stick below the knuckles, out of sight from above
the fingers close over the stick from above
brief.caption: German grip: the back of the hand up, knuckles on top, the thumb tucked at the side of the stick.
brief.alt: A hand seen from above holding a drumstick palm down, knuckles up.

cases.name: index fingers straight along the sticks, a subtle wrong brief
cases.note: Was 'fulcrum at the butt end' in the first set; that brief claimed where the hands sat along sticks whose ends the hands cover, which no photograph can settle.
cases.failsOn: Both index fingers visibly curl around their sticks; the brief says each lies straight out along the top of its stick, not curled.

brief.subject: Both hands holding drumsticks with the index fingers extended straight along the sticks
mustShow: both hands hold their stick with the backs of the hands up
each index finger lies straight out along the top of its stick, pointing toward the tip, not curled around it
the other fingers close around the stick beneath the straight index finger
brief.caption: Matched grip with the index fingers pointing straight down the sticks.
brief.alt: Two hands holding drumsticks, each index finger extended straight along the top of its stick.
